title: Direct web redirects escape the authorized scope
execution_path: CLI web --direct -> authorize initial target -> HttpTransport.get -> urllib redirect -> unapproved destination
evidence: HttpTransport uses urllib.request.urlopen with the default redirect handler after WebReconOrchestrator authorizes only the initial target. A safe two-loopback-server probe confirmed the second server was contacted (redirect_followed=True).
impact: An allowed service can cause Argus to contact a denied public, link-local, loopback, metadata, or other destination and return its content to analysis/reporting.
abuse_scenario: An in-scope web server returns a 302 to a cloud metadata or sensitive internal URL; Argus follows it without another guardrail decision.
existing_protection: The initial literal IPv4 target is checked by authorize_host.
protection_gap: Redirect destinations, resolved peers, and the final connected address are never re-authorized.
recommendation: Disable redirects by default or resolve and authorize every hop and final peer under one canonical target policy; bound and audit the redirect chain.
regression_tests: Cross-host redirect is denied before the second connection
Link-local, loopback, hostname, mapped-IPv6, cross-scheme, rebinding, and multi-address redirects fail closed
Explicitly permitted same-host redirects record every hop

title: The web console is an unauthenticated live-control plane
category: Access control and agent control plane
execution_path: HTTP JSON -> Pydantic request -> process-local scan lock -> live scanner/host/AD action -> shared reports
evidence: The application has no authentication, authorization, rate limit, CSRF/origin protection, enforced bind address, run ownership, or approval-token verification. /api/scan accepts arm and dry_run=false; /api/host and /api/ad accept credentials and run live collectors.
impact: Any reachable client can launch scans, submit credentials, spend AI budget, overwrite reports, and read results.
abuse_scenario: A network peer or XSS payload sends a same-origin request that starts a live or armed-listed scan and retrieves the response.
existing_protection: Pydantic parses requests, a process-local lock serializes work, and literal targets are scope checked.
protection_gap: These controls do not identify the caller or authorize the action; binding to loopback is documented but not enforced.
recommendation: Enforce loopback-only demo mode and implement authenticated, role/action-authorized service mode with centralized approvals, CSRF/origin, limits, durable run ownership, and safe secret input.
regression_tests: Unauthenticated requests cannot start or read runs
Live, armed, and credentialed actions require action-bound approval
Non-loopback startup fails without secure service configuration

title: Untrusted scanner and model output executes as browser script
execution_path: Scanner/parser/model output -> API result -> string interpolation -> element.innerHTML
evidence: Errors, executive summaries, paths, findings, assets, and evidence are interpolated into innerHTML without escaping or a CSP backstop.
impact: An in-scope banner/page or model response can execute JavaScript in the operator console, read data, and drive same-origin live API actions.
abuse_scenario: A malicious web banner becomes finding evidence containing an event-handler payload that runs when the result is displayed.
existing_protection: Some scanner text passes the regex sanitizer.
protection_gap: The sanitizer is not an HTML sanitizer and output remains attacker/model controlled.
recommendation: Use textContent and safe DOM construction, strictly sanitize any intentional markup, and add restrictive CSP and browser security headers.
regression_tests: Every response field renders hostile tags and event attributes literally
Scanner and model XSS corpus cannot issue API requests

title: SSH host collection permits option injection and exposes credentials
execution_path: Web/CLI host input -> SSHCreds -> authorize target/check only -> sshpass/ssh argv in helper container
evidence: The password is passed with sshpass -p, username is concatenated into user@target without validation or option termination, authorize_host skips argument hygiene, and StrictHostKeyChecking/UserKnownHostsFile are disabled.
impact: A crafted username can change SSH options within the helper container; passwords are visible in process arguments and man-in-the-middle hosts are accepted.
abuse_scenario: A reachable web caller supplies an option-like SSH username that changes SSH behavior while the supplied password is exposed to other container processes.
existing_protection: Targets and closed audit-check keys are scoped and the remote command comes from a fixed catalog.
protection_gap: User identity and credential transport are constructed outside the argument guard and host authenticity is explicitly disabled.
recommendation: Use a maintained SSH library or secret-safe agent/file-descriptor transport, strict username schema and option termination, fixed configuration, and verified host keys/pins.
regression_tests: Option-like and control-character usernames are rejected
Passwords never appear in argv, logs, reports, or errors

title: Secret and PHI sanitization does not support the product claims
execution_path: Collector/error/model data -> regex sanitizer -> AI, audit, reports, and web UI
evidence: Only simple password, SSN, and MRN regexes exist. Safe probes missed JSON passwords, Authorization Bearer, cookies, API keys, connection URIs, multiline passwords, and private-key markers.
impact: Credentials, tokens, PHI, directory data, and keys can be sent to cloud models or persisted/displayed.
abuse_scenario: A scanner returns an Authorization header or JSON credential; Argus sends it to a cloud provider and writes it to a report unchanged.
existing_protection: Three regex patterns sanitize selected observation fields before some downstream processing.
protection_gap: Coverage is unstructured and incomplete, and errors/model output/encodings/multiline values are not consistently sanitized.
recommendation: Implement typed field-level classification, structured redaction and secret detection at every egress/persistence sink, protected raw evidence, minimization, and retention controls.
regression_tests: Comprehensive secret/PHI corpus is absent at AI, audit, API, JSON, CSV, and Markdown sinks
Encoded, structured, multiline, split, and exception forms are covered

title: Audit logging is not durable, concurrent, or truncation-evident by default
execution_path: Guardrail authorize/record -> in-memory previous hash -> append file -> optional local JSON anchor
evidence: A valid-prefix truncation still verifies true without an anchor; two initialized writers fork the chain. State replay skips malformed lines. Writes/anchors lack locks, transaction, fsync, atomic coordination, permission/link checks, and an authenticated remote receipt.
impact: Concurrent runs and crashes can corrupt or roll back audit history, and default verification cannot establish complete forensic history.
abuse_scenario: Two web workers authorize concurrently and produce a broken chain, or a valid suffix is deleted and verify still returns true.
existing_protection: Entries use HMAC-SHA256 chaining with a minimum key length and optional tip cross-check.
protection_gap: Cryptographic records do not serialize writers, prove completeness, or make a same-privilege local pathname immutable.
recommendation: Use a transactional append service/store with monotonic sequence, locking, durable atomic commits, strict file/link controls, recovery/rotation, and independently authenticated append-only anchor receipts.
regression_tests: Multi-process stress yields one valid chain
Crash between log and anchor recovers or fails closed
Malformed, permission, symlink, and anchor-outage cases alert

title: The bundled isolation verifier can report success without testing isolation
execution_path: Operator runs verifier -> temporary internal-network container -> install/test commands -> human interprets output
evidence: The verifier tries to install tools from an internal network that cannot reach package repositories, suppresses failures, can treat missing ping/nslookup as blocked, does not aggregate assertions into a failing status, and omits host gateway, TCP, IPv6, DNS, and shared-network checks.
impact: Operators may run packet-emitting tools based on a false green isolation result.
abuse_scenario: A route to the host/LAN exists, but the verifier lacks its test binary and prints a blocked-style result instead of failing.
existing_protection: Compose defines an internal network and avoids Docker socket, host network, privileged mode, and host mounts.
protection_gap: Static intent is not runtime proof, and the supplied proof script cannot distinguish missing prerequisites from denied routes.
recommendation: Use a pinned verifier image with built-in tools; test effective routes/capabilities from the actual attacker container and fail on missing prerequisites or any host/LAN/internet/DNS/IPv6 reachability.
regression_tests: Each deliberately introduced route leak exits nonzero
Host gateway, host.docker.internal, LAN, internet, DNS, IPv6, and TCP are checked

title: Attack-path observed status is not evidence-correct
execution_path: Observations/findings -> global keyword or graph correlation -> observed attack path -> report
evidence: V1 rules use global substring/co-occurrence rather than typed ordered per-asset prerequisites; unrelated assets can form relay or privilege chains. Shadow-AI/segmentation paths can be marked observed without abuse/pivot proof, and V2 creates random duplicate path nodes.
impact: Reports can assert attack chains that never occurred and misdirect remediation or compliance decisions.
abuse_scenario: TLS weakness on A, SMB weakness on B, and AD evidence on C produce an observed relay path despite no connected topology.
existing_protection: Deterministic rules attach proof labels and V2 has an EvidenceGraph abstraction.
protection_gap: Rules lack stable provenance IDs, topology, temporal/run boundaries, typed prerequisites, and proof-state transitions.
recommendation: Implement immutable evidence IDs, asset/topology edges, prerequisite DAGs, run/temporal scope, dedupe, confidence, and hypothesis/supported/verified states advanced only by collectors.
regression_tests: Cross-asset relay and privilege scenarios remain hypotheses
Missing prerequisite paths are not observed
Every path edge cites immutable source evidence

title: Approval tokens are replayable and insufficiently action-bound
execution_path: Operator mint -> token output -> selected CLI verify -> mode action
evidence: Tokens bind modes, canonical targets, and expiry but have no nonce/consumption ledger, operator/run/action/profile/sandbox/policy hash, issued-at/max TTL, or key separation. One token verified twice; web paths do not use it.
impact: Captured approvals can be reused until expiry or survive changes to the action the operator intended to review.
abuse_scenario: A token approved for a target class is replayed after profile/policy/sandbox changes or consumed concurrently.
existing_protection: HMAC construction, canonical target/mode sets, and expiry are sound basics.
protection_gap: The capability is reusable and represents only a broad mode/target set, not an exact execution.
recommendation: Use a dedicated key, exact immutable action digest, nonce, issuer/operator, issued-at/max TTL, and atomic consumption; enforce it centrally across all interfaces.

title: Continuous mode is non-operational scaffolding
execution_path: Unexposed loop -> load graph -> propose -> authorize only -> correlate/delta -> overwrite JSON -> sleep
evidence: No public entry point exists; proposals commonly lack targets and are skipped; run_authorized does not execute or add evidence; persistence is non-atomic/schema-less; exceptions are swallowed; no locks, recovery, alerts, health, metrics, retention, or multi-instance safety exist.
impact: The advertised 24/7 sensor can silently do no useful collection, lose state, duplicate paths, and miss alerts.
abuse_scenario: A collector error is swallowed, state overwrite is interrupted, and subsequent cycles continue with incomplete/corrupt evidence and no operator alert.
existing_protection: The loop calls guardrail authorization and persists a graph snapshot.
protection_gap: Authorization is not execution and a JSON sleep loop is not an operable durable service.
recommendation: Reclassify as experimental, then design durable run/evidence state, real guarded collectors, leases/supervision, idempotency, recovery, alert delivery, health/metrics, retention, and migrations.

title: PoC gates do not technically isolate execution and two probes fabricate proof
execution_path: Direct PoC function -> armed/env/network-string gates -> host socket -> proof result
evidence: The lab gate is an environment assertion; default probes use host sockets. Mapped IPv6 host splitting is broken. SMB writable and anonymous LDAP checks only connect to TCP ports but claim ACL/RootDSE proof.
impact: Direct callers can emit packets without attested sandboxing and reports can upgrade reachability into access that was never verified.
abuse_scenario: An open 445 port is reported as write permission confirmed even though no ACL or SMB protocol operation occurred.
existing_protection: Armed, lab-address, attestation, catalog, and guardrail scope gates exist.
protection_gap: The gates express operator intent, not technical execution location, and the probes do not implement their named protocol assertions.
recommendation: Execute a sealed action in an attested sandbox and implement safe protocol-specific states for reachable/authenticated/authorized/proven.
regression_tests: Mapped IPv6 and non-lab routes fail
All gates and proof state are audited

title: Tool authorization is not bound to executable identity
execution_path: Logical tool name -> guardrail -> independently supplied argv[0] -> PATH resolution -> process
evidence: The firewall validates a logical string, while sandbox execution trusts argv[0]/PATH; no invariant binds ToolSpec to resolved realpath/image digest. Docker is PATH-resolved, arbitrary armed names can be allowed, and read_only/needs_root metadata is unused.
impact: A hostile PATH/symlink/wrapper or direct internal caller can execute a program different from the audited logical tool.
abuse_scenario: A malicious executable earlier on PATH uses an allowlisted name and receives the scanner arguments.
existing_protection: Normal V1 uses a fixed registry, argv-only subprocess calls, and a default-deny logical allowlist.
protection_gap: Name authorization does not verify the program artifact that the OS/container executes.
recommendation: Authorize immutable ToolSpec/action IDs, construct argv after authorization, resolve/pin trusted executable or image identity, use a fixed environment, and enforce impact/privilege metadata.
regression_tests: PATH, symlink, absolute, relative, and wrapper substitutions fail

title: Collector errors and tool absence are frequently converted into empty evidence
execution_path: Tool/provider call -> nonzero/timeout/exception -> parser/fallback -> apparently normal result
evidence: Parsers can process stdout after failure; stderr is not structured; AD ignores missing/nonzero states; web maps exceptions to status 0; model failures silently fall back; continuous exceptions are swallowed.
impact: No findings can mean clean, unavailable, unauthenticated, timed out, malformed, or degraded, causing false assurance.
abuse_scenario: ldapsearch is missing, the AD collector returns no observations, and the report is interpreted as a clean directory assessment.
existing_protection: ExecResult includes exit, timeout, stderr, and tool_missing and some missing tools append errors.
protection_gap: Downstream collectors and reports do not consistently preserve these states or completeness.
recommendation: Use typed success/partial/timeout/missing/auth/parse/unsupported outcomes, fail or mark incomplete explicitly, and audit/alert all degradation.
regression_tests: Each failure type has a distinct API/report/audit state
Partial stdout is handled by explicit policy

title: Sandbox execution lacks resource bounds and per-run isolation
execution_path: Authorized action -> shared long-lived attacker container -> buffered subprocess -> result
evidence: communicate buffers unlimited output; attacker is long-lived/root with NET_RAW/NET_ADMIN, no read-only FS, cap drop, no-new-privileges, pids/CPU/memory/file/output limits, or per-run container. Runs share state.
impact: Verbose/forking/malicious tools can exhaust resources, retain artifacts, contaminate runs, or amplify escape impact.
abuse_scenario: A tool emits unbounded output and exhausts host memory before parser/body truncation is applied.
existing_protection: Internal network, no host mounts/socket/host network, argv-only execution, timeout, and process-group kill reduce risk.
protection_gap: Network topology and timeout do not bound memory, CPU, process count, filesystem state, privileges, or cross-run contamination.
recommendation: Use ephemeral non-root per-run containers, minimal capabilities, read-only root/tmpfs quotas, seccomp/AppArmor, no-new-privileges, resource limits, streaming byte caps, cancellation, and cleanup verification.
regression_tests: Timeout and cancellation leave no processes

title: AI output lacks strict schema and evidence provenance enforcement
execution_path: Sanitized observations -> Ollama/Anthropic -> permissive JSON parsing -> findings/correlation/report
evidence: The parser accepts aliases, single objects, defaults, invalid values and extra content; some shapes crash. Correlation accepts arbitrary JSON and labels it trusted. Output is not post-sanitized or linked to observation IDs.
impact: Prompt-injected or malformed output can fabricate assets/evidence/severity and inject report/UI content, though it cannot directly authorize V1 tools.
abuse_scenario: A banner tells the model to invent a Critical finding for another asset; permissive parsing accepts it without a collected evidence ID.
existing_protection: System prompts identify untrusted data and deterministic V1 code retains authorization control; provider failures fall back.
protection_gap: Prompts are not schema or provenance enforcement and fallback visibility is weak.
recommendation: Use strict versioned schemas, enums/bounds/reject-unknown, observation-ID citations, asset/scope reconciliation, post-model redaction, and explicit untrusted model status.
regression_tests: Malformed and unknown fields are rejected
Fabricated/out-of-scope assets and evidence are rejected

title: Reports are shared, non-atomic, and injection-prone
execution_path: Scan result -> fixed JSON/CSV/Markdown paths -> browser/spreadsheet/Markdown consumer
evidence: Runs overwrite fixed filenames with direct non-atomic writes and have no ID, ownership, cross-process lock, permissions/retention policy, or post-model redaction. CSV formulas and Markdown active content are not neutralized.
impact: Concurrent/crashed runs can mix or truncate reports; users can see other runs; downstream viewers can execute formulas or active content.
abuse_scenario: A finding title beginning with a spreadsheet formula is opened in Excel, or two workers overwrite one report concurrently.
existing_protection: Standard JSON and CSV serializers are used and a process-local web lock serializes one process.
protection_gap: Serialization alone does not provide atomicity, tenancy, safe presentation, or cross-process coordination.
recommendation: Use per-run immutable owned storage, atomic writes and integrity metadata, safe serializers/formula neutralization, sanitization, retention, and encryption as required.
regression_tests: Concurrent/crash writes do not mix or truncate
CSV and Markdown payloads remain inert

title: Container and tool supply chain is mutable and weakly verified
execution_path: Docker build/pull -> mutable image/packages/download/templates -> scanner execution
evidence: Kali rolling and multiple latest images are used; apt packages are unpinned; Nuclei download lacks checksum/signature and install failure is tolerated; templates/tool behavior are not version locked; CI does not build/scan/SBOM/sign containers.
impact: The same source commit can execute different or compromised tools/templates and produce non-reproducible findings/side effects.
abuse_scenario: A mutable upstream image or binary download changes behavior while source and Python lock remain unchanged.
existing_protection: Python requirements are hash locked and GitHub Actions are SHA pinned; an application SBOM is generated.
protection_gap: Those controls do not cover base images, OS packages, downloaded binaries, templates, or runtime identities.
recommendation: Pin image digests and package/tool/template versions/hashes/signatures; fail installation closed; build, scan, SBOM and sign images; record component identity in every run.

title: Dependency, packaging, and current CI state are not release-valid
execution_path: Clean checkout -> hash-locked install/build -> tests or installed CLI/assets
evidence: A fresh locked install produced 97 passes and 2 NetworkX import failures, matching current main CI. A clean build produced aegis 0.0.0 without dependencies, console entry point, static UI, policy, or Compose assets; runtime output can also confuse package discovery.
impact: Clean CI/developer installs fail and a successfully built wheel is not a functional product artifact.
abuse_scenario: A user installs the wheel expecting Argus and receives an incomplete 0.0.0 library whose default policy/static assets and CLI are absent.
existing_protection: The lock is hash checked, tests run in CI, and source-tree execution works in a pre-populated environment.
protection_gap: Dependencies and package metadata/assets have multiple inconsistent sources and the built artifact is never smoke tested.
recommendation: Adopt one authoritative project/lock workflow, declare runtime/optional dependencies, package data and entry points, exclude outputs, and install/test the wheel in CI.
regression_tests: Clean locked install passes all tests
Installed-wheel smoke runs outside source tree

title: Scope and policy parsing has representation and validation gaps
execution_path: Input/policy string -> repeated target extraction/canonical check -> original argv and audit string
evidence: URL parsing is delimiter based and mishandles IPv6/user-info; IPv6 and DNS are unsupported while resolve_dns is configured; policy lacks strict schema/version validation; special network/broadcast addresses in allowed CIDRs are accepted; canonical checks are not propagated to execution.
impact: Operator intent and effective behavior can diverge and future feature changes can reopen ambiguous target bypasses.
abuse_scenario: A target representation is approved in one layer but the original representation is interpreted differently by a downstream tool.
existing_protection: Ambiguous IPv4 leading-zero and host-bit forms fail, broad CIDRs are limited, and hostnames currently deny.
protection_gap: There is no single validated target value or versioned policy schema shared by approval, guardrail, execution, and audit.
recommendation: Create a strict versioned policy and canonical AuthorizedTarget containing parsed scheme/host/port/network/resolved peers/special-address policy, used end to end.
regression_tests: Executed and audited target exactly matches authorized object

title: Parsers and output handling are insufficiently bounded and hardened
execution_path: Untrusted subprocess/XML/HTTP output -> full in-memory capture -> parser -> observation
evidence: Full process output is buffered before truncation; parsers accept arbitrary version/localization/size data; stdlib XML is a silent fallback when defusedxml is absent; exit/stderr are inconsistently incorporated; fuzz/size/binary tests are sparse.
impact: Crafted output can exhaust memory, crash parsing, generate false evidence, or invoke unsafe XML behavior in a degraded environment.
abuse_scenario: A service/tool emits massive or malformed output, exhausting the process before the 200/4096-character presentation cap applies.
existing_protection: Some stored fields and HTTP bodies are truncated, timeouts exist, and defusedxml is preferred.
protection_gap: Limits apply after ingestion and the secure parser dependency can fail open.
recommendation: Stream with hard byte/record limits, require secure parser dependencies, use parser schemas and typed errors, and add fuzz/property/version corpora.
regression_tests: Nonzero and stderr produce explicit incomplete/error states

title: Documentation and test-count claims are materially stale
execution_path: Documentation/badges/commands -> operator installation and safety decision
evidence: Documents cite 39, 72, 75, or 81 tests while 99 collect; the documented short audit key causes 12 failures; clean lock has two failures; multiple read-only/privacy/isolation/audit/continuous/PoC claims exceed code.
impact: Users cannot reproduce advertised checks and may make unsafe deployment decisions.
abuse_scenario: An operator interprets a proven-isolated/read-only/24x7 claim as deployment approval despite absent enforcement.
existing_protection: The repository contains extensive design and security documentation.
protection_gap: Claims and snippets are not generated or executed as release gates.
recommendation: Make commands/claims executable CI checks, generate badges/counts from CI, and link every security claim to invariant evidence and an owner.
regression_tests: README commands pass from clean checkout
Badges derive from current required CI
Security claims inventory has automated or explicit verification status

title: Aegis/Argus and V1/V2 duplication obscures the supported architecture
execution_path: Contributor/operator chooses package, command, V1/V2 model, or configuration path
evidence: Product docs say Argus while package/CLI/env/tickets remain Aegis; two Observation models and correlation approaches coexist; V2 is disconnected; policy permits tools absent from registry.
impact: Contributors can harden or extend the wrong path and security properties diverge across nominally equivalent subsystems.
abuse_scenario: A security fix lands in the V2 EvidenceGraph while production V1 reports still use the unrelated linear Observation/chains path.
existing_protection: Modules are separated and current V1 runtime is still identifiable by tracing CLI imports.
protection_gap: There is no ADR/stability boundary/deprecation plan that declares the authoritative architecture.
recommendation: Publish an ADR for the supported path, isolate/version experimental APIs, stage a naming and evidence migration, and remove dead configuration after compatibility review.
regression_tests: Compatibility aliases and deprecations are tested
Experimental APIs are isolated and versioned

title: CI omits important quality and security gates
execution_path: Pull request -> workflow checks -> merge/release decision
evidence: CI runs tests, dependency audit, Bandit, SBOM, and informational secret scan but not Ruff, mypy, coverage threshold, installed wheel, container build/scan/SBOM, license checks, or Python matrix. Ruff reports 27 and mypy 34 errors.
impact: Broken or unreleasable main revisions can coexist with several green security jobs and quality drift accumulates.
abuse_scenario: A dependency/package/type/container regression merges because the relevant local-only or absent check is not required.
existing_protection: Actions are SHA pinned; tests, dependency audit, Bandit, and SBOM are useful blocking checks.
protection_gap: There is no complete defined release gate and secret scanning is informational/working-tree-only.
recommendation: Add staged blocking lint/type/coverage/package/container/license gates, supported-Python matrix, artifacts/SARIF, history-aware secret scanning, and branch protection.
regression_tests: Clean PR installs/tests across supported Python
Coverage and policy gates reject known violations
Branch protection requires all release checks

title: Open-source and release-governance claims lack required artifacts
execution_path: Repository/package/release -> user legal, support, upgrade, and provenance decision
evidence: No LICENSE, changelog, release/version policy, artifact signing/provenance, or supported-version/security-disclosure lifecycle exists; wheel version defaults to 0.0.0.
impact: Users lack legal permission clarity, trustworthy upgrade history, provenance, and a vulnerability-reporting contract.
abuse_scenario: An organization deploys the public code believing it is licensed/open-source but cannot establish rights or artifact provenance.
existing_protection: The repository is public and CI produces an SBOM.
protection_gap: Public availability and an SBOM do not grant a license or establish release/support integrity.
recommendation: Select an approved license, add security/support/changelog/version policies, dependency/license review, and reproducible signed releases with provenance.
regression_tests: Disclosure contact and supported versions are published
